title: Kale (Sukuma Wiki) — East Africa Vegetable Guide
content:
## Kale / Sukuma Wiki (Brassica oleracea acephala)

Sukuma wiki is the most widely consumed leafy vegetable in urban and peri-urban East Africa.

### Varieties

- **Mfalme F1** — hybrid, high yield, 60 days to first harvest
- **Collards Southern Georgia** — traditional OPV
- **Thousand Headed** — long harvesting period

### Planting

- Can be direct seeded or nursery raised
- Spacing: 30cm × 30cm (or 30cm × 45cm for large varieties)
- Harvest leaves from bottom up — plant continues producing 3–6 months
- Succession plant every 3 weeks for continuous supply

### Fertilizer

- Compost or well-decomposed manure 10 t/ha before planting
- CAN topdress 100 kg/ha at 3 weeks and 6 weeks

### Pests and Diseases

- **Diamondback moth:** Bt spray or Spinetoram
- **Aphids:** Neem or Dimethoate
- **Black rot / downy mildew:** Crop rotation; avoid overhead irrigation
content_sw:
## Sukuma Wiki (Brassica oleracea)

Sukuma wiki ni mboga inayoliwa zaidi mijini Afrika Mashariki.

### Upanzi

- Umbali sentimita 30 × 30
- Vuna majani kutoka chini kwenda juu — mmea unaendelea miezi 3–6

### Mbolea

- Mbolea ya asili tani 10/hekta; CAN kilo 100/hekta wiki 3 na 6

title: Sweet Potato — Food Security and Drought Crop
content:
## Sweet Potato (Ipomoea batatas)

Sweet potato is a key food security crop — vines survive drought and roots store well.

### Varieties

- **Kenya varieties:** Kabode (OFSP — high beta-carotene), Kenspot 1, Mugande
- **Orange-fleshed (OFSP):** Combats vitamin A deficiency — promoted by CIP/KALRO
- **White-fleshed:** Higher dry matter for processing

### Planting

- Propagate from vine cuttings (30cm length), not tubers
- Plant at 30° angle, 2/3 buried; spacing 30cm × 90cm
- Plant at onset of rains; mounds in heavy clay improve drainage
- Maturity: 3–5 months depending on variety

### Yield

- 10–15 t/ha roots under good management; vines also used as livestock feed
content_sw:
## Viazi Vitamu (Ipomoea batatas)

Viazi vitamu ni zao la usalama wa chakula — vinastahimili ukame.

### Aina

- **Kabode (OFSP)** — rangi ya machungwa, vitamini A
- **Kenspot 1, Mugande** — Kenya

### Upanzi

- Panda kwa makata ya matawi sentimita 30; umbali 30 × 90
- Mavuno: miezi 3–5

title: Banana and Plantain — East Africa Production
content:
## Banana (Musa spp.) — East Africa

Banana is a staple in Uganda (matoke), western Kenya, and Tanzania highlands.

### Varieties

- **East African Highland Banana (EAHB / matoke):** Cooking type; Uganda, western Kenya
- **Cavendish (Grand Nain):** Dessert/export; Central Kenya
- **FHIA 17, FHIA 23:** Improved cooking/dessert hybrids

### Planting

- Use disease-free tissue culture seedlings from certified nurseries
- Spacing: 3m × 3m (≈1110 plants/ha)
- Hole size: 60cm × 60cm × 60cm filled with topsoil + manure
- First harvest: 12–15 months

### Key Diseases

- **Banana Xanthomonas Wilt (BXW):** Remove entire mat (corm + pseudostem); disinfect tools; no cure
- **Fusarium wilt (Panama disease):** Use resistant varieties; avoid moving infected soil
- **Black Sigatoka:** Mancozeb + oil spray program in export plantations
content_sw:
## Ndizi (Musa spp.)

Ndizi ni chakula cha msingi Uganda (matoke) na magharibi Kenya.

### Aina

- **EAHB / matoke** — za kupikia
- **Cavendish** — za kula mbivu

### Magonjwa

- **BXW:** Ng'oa mzizi mzima; hakuna tiba — chanja zana
- **Fusarium:** Tumia aina zinazostahimili

title: Groundnut (Peanut) — Oil and Protein Crop
content:
## Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea)

Groundnut is an important oil and protein legume in eastern and southern Africa.

### Varieties

- **ICGV-SM 90704, CG 7** — ICRISAT releases; drought tolerant
- **Red Valencia** — popular local type in Kenya/Tanzania

### Planting

- Plant in well-drained sandy loam — does not tolerate waterlogging
- Spacing: 45cm × 15cm; seed rate 80–100 kg/ha
- Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation on new fields
- Calcium is critical for pod filling — apply gypsum 200 kg/ha on sandy soils

### Harvest

- Dig when leaves yellow and inner shell is dark (not white)
- Dry pods to 8% moisture before storage to prevent aflatoxin
content_sw:
## Njugu Karanga (Arachis hypogaea)

Njugu ni zao la mafuta na protini Afrika mashariki.

### Upanzi

- Udongo wa mchanga unaodrain vizuri
- Umbali sentimita 45 × 15
- Weka gypsum kilo 200/hekta kwenye udongo wa mchanga kwa pod vizuri

title: Soybean — Protein and Soil Fertility Crop
content:
## Soybean (Glycine max)

Soybean is expanding in East Africa for human nutrition, animal feed, and crop rotation.

### Varieties

- **SB 19, SB 24** — Kenya releases; 90–110 days
- **Maksoy 3N** — Uganda

### Planting

- Inoculate seed with Bradyrhizobium japonicum before planting
- Spacing: 50cm × 5cm; seed rate 60–80 kg/ha
- Plant at onset of rains; do not waterlog

### Uses

- Human consumption (soy milk, tofu, mixed flour)
- Livestock feed (soybean meal)
- Nitrogen fixation improves soil for following maize crop — 40–60 kg N/ha equivalent
content_sw:
## Soya (Glycine max)

Soya inapanuka Afrika Mashariki kwa lishe na mzunguko wa mazao.

### Upanzi

- Chanja mbegu na Bradyrhizobium kabla ya kupanda
- Umbali sentimita 50 × 5
- Inafuga nitrojeni — nzuri kabla ya mahindi
